clean: Dropup (lens: state truth and variant integrity): dropup--light-1280, dropup--dark-1280, dropup--light-390, dropup--dark-390. The menu is open above the toggle. It starts at the toggle's start edge with a gap of about 2px, matching `.dropup .dropdown-menu[data-bs-popper] { top: auto; bottom: 100%; margin-bottom: var(--bs-dropdown-spacer) }`. The caret points up. No menu item is hovered, focused, or active, and the toggle shows no focus ring and no active fill. The width variants are pixel-equivalent in layout. The light and dark variants differ only in the page, menu surface, border, and text colors, apart from the low-confidence toggle-fill note.

Dropup center (lens: state truth and variant integrity): dropup-center--light-1280, dropup-center--dark-1280, dropup-center--light-390, dropup-center--dark-390. The menu is open above the toggle and starts at the toggle's start edge. The scenario markup sets `data-bs-popper="static"` (app/browser/constants.ts, the 'Dropup center' entry). Bootstrap applies centering only through Popper in js/src/dropdown.js (CLASS_NAME_DROPUP_CENTER), and scss/_dropdown.scss gives `.dropup-center` nothing except `position: relative`. In static mode Bootstrap therefore also renders this start-aligned menu under the `.dropup` rule. Centering is NOT-EVIDENCED by this portfolio, by design of the static scenario, and is not a defect. No item or toggle interaction state shows. The variants agree.

Dropend (lens: state truth and variant integrity): dropend--light-1280, dropend--dark-1280, dropend--light-390, dropend--dark-390. The menu is open on the end side, with its top aligned to the toggle top and a gap of about 2px, matching `.dropend .dropdown-menu[data-bs-popper] { top: 0; left: 100%; margin-left: var(--bs-dropdown-spacer) }`. The caret points right, sits on the baseline, and is drawn in `::after`. No hover, focus, or active state shows. The 1280 and 390 layouts are identical. The light and dark variants differ only in the theme surfaces.

Dropstart (lens: state truth and variant integrity): dropstart--light-1280, dropstart--dark-1280, dropstart--light-390, dropstart--dark-390. The menu is open on the start side, with its top aligned to the toggle and a gap of about 2px, matching `.dropstart .dropdown-menu[data-bs-popper] { top: 0; right: 100%; margin-right: var(--bs-dropdown-spacer) }`. The caret points left, sits before the label in `::before`, and no `::after` caret appears. No hover, focus, or active state shows. The toggle's horizontal position differs between 1280 and 390 only because of the `col-6 offset-6` column, which is a change the width must make. The menu-to-toggle relation is identical at both widths. The light and dark variants differ only in the theme surfaces.

clean: Dropup (dropup--light-1280, dropup--dark-1280, dropup--light-390, dropup--dark-390): The menu opens above the toggle with its start edge on the toggle's start edge. The gap is about 2px, which matches .dropup .dropdown-menu[data-bs-popper] (bottom: 100%; margin-bottom: var(--bs-dropdown-spacer), where $dropdown-spacer is .125rem). The caret points up (caret(up): border-bottom .3em solid, with side borders transparent). The menu is 160px wide (min-width 10rem), about 82px tall (8px padding-y plus two 32px items plus 1px borders), and its item text is inset 16px. The radius is about 6px. The light border is black at 17.5% and the dark border is white at 15%. There is no shadow, because $enable-shadows is false.

Dropup center (dropup-center--light-1280, dropup-center--dark-1280, dropup-center--light-390, dropup-center--dark-390): The markup is 'dropup-center dropup' with data-bs-popper="static". In that markup the release's stylesheet gives .dropup-center only position: relative, and the .dropup [data-bs-popper] rule sets left: 0 and bottom: 100%. The start-aligned menu above the toggle, the 2px spacer, and the up caret therefore match what the release paints for this static markup. Centering happens only through Popper's inline transform, which this markup does not invoke.

Dropend (dropend--light-1280, dropend--dark-1280, dropend--light-390, dropend--dark-390): The menu opens to the end of the toggle with its top on the toggle's top edge. The gap is about 2px, which matches .dropend [data-bs-popper] (top: 0; left: 100%; margin-left: spacer). The caret points right and sits at vertical-align 0 (caret(end) with ::after vertical-align: 0). The menu box, border, radius, and item spacing match the dropup reading.

Dropstart (dropstart--light-1280, dropstart--dark-1280, dropstart--light-390, dropstart--dark-390): The menu opens to the start side of the toggle with its top on the toggle's top edge. The gap is about 2px, which matches .dropstart [data-bs-popper] (top: 0; right: 100%; margin-right: spacer). A single left-pointing caret precedes the label, on ::before at vertical-align 0, and no ::after caret paints. The menu box, border, radius, and item spacing match the dropup reading.

reviewed: Lane held: the Bootstrap 5.3.8 fidelity lens named in the dispatch (rendered-surface review), not the default subjective design-fit lane.

findings.region: The stacked link list under the brand. The third link, 'Scroll depots', sits at about y=139.
findings.seen: 'Scroll depots' is painted near-white, visibly brighter than its non-active siblings 'Scroll routes' and 'Scroll couriers'. Those two are at the muted navbar color. It is close to the active 'Scroll home' but not equal to it. The light-390 twin paints all three non-active links the same grey.
findings.expected: Bootstrap paints every non-active, non-hovered `.navbar-nav .nav-link` at `--bs-navbar-color`. In `_navbar.scss` the `.navbar` rule sets `--bs-navbar-color: rgba(var(--bs-emphasis-color-rgb), .65)`, and the `.navbar-nav` rule maps `--bs-nav-link-color` to that variable. In dark mode that value is 65% white, and all three non-active links match. Only `:hover` or `:focus` takes `--bs-navbar-hover-color` (80%), and only `.active` or `.show` takes the active color. The markup puts no state class on 'Scroll depots'. The brightness matches the hover color, so the likely cause is a leftover pointer hover in the capture, not the partial. Veneer `_navbar.scss` has no rule that sets one link apart by theme. Referral to the Orchestrator: re-capture with the pointer parked outside the subject.

findings.region: The second stacked link, 'Dark routes', at about y=103 inside the dark card.
findings.seen: 'Dark routes' is painted a light grey that is brighter than the same link in navbar-inverted--light-1280.png and in both 390 variants. The 390 variants paint it at the dimmer 55% white.
findings.expected: The subject is forced dark by `data-bs-theme="dark"` on both the card and the nav. Bootstrap's `.navbar[data-bs-theme="dark"]` rule sets `--bs-navbar-color` to `$navbar-dark-color`, which is `rgba($white, .55)`. That value does not depend on the page theme, so the light-1280 and dark-1280 frames must paint 'Dark routes' identically at 55% white. Only `:hover` or `:focus` raises it to `$navbar-dark-hover-color` (75%). The brighter paint matches that hover value, so the likely cause is a pointer left over the link during capture. Referral to the Orchestrator on the capture instrument.

findings.region: The second stacked link, 'Dark class routes', at about y=103 inside the dark card.
findings.seen: 'Dark class routes' is painted brighter than the same link in navbar-inverted-class--light-1280.png and in both 390 variants. Those frames paint it at the muted 55% white.
findings.expected: Bootstrap's `.navbar-dark` rule sets `--bs-navbar-color: rgba($white, .55)` whatever the page theme, even with `data-bs-theme="light"` on the nav, because the class writes white literals. The non-hovered link must therefore match the light-1280 twin. The brighter paint matches `$navbar-dark-hover-color` (75% white), which is the same hover-residue pattern as navbar-inverted--dark-1280. Referral to the Orchestrator: re-capture with the pointer parked outside the subject.

clean: Navbar scroll, light-1280 and dark-1280: the `navbar-expand-lg` bar lays out in one row with no toggler. The brand has the 0.75rem container-fluid inset and the 1rem end margin. The links carry the 0.5rem inline padding. The active link is at full emphasis, black in light mode and white in dark mode. The other links are at 65% emphasis, and the bar has no background of its own.

Navbar scroll, light-390: the bar is collapsed with the `show` collapse open. The brand sits left and the toggler right, with a 1px border at 15% emphasis, the 0.375rem radius, and a 1.5em icon. The links stack flush with the brand's left edge. Active and muted colors match the release.

Navbar scroll, dark-390: the layout, toggler, and the colors of the active link and of 'Scroll routes' and 'Scroll couriers' match the release. Only the 'Scroll depots' hover-like paint is out of line, as the findings record.

Navbar inverted (data-bs-theme attribute), light-1280, light-390, and dark-390: the dark card has the translucent-white border and radius, and the bar sits flush inside it. The brand is white. The toggler has a white icon and a border at 10% white. The active link is white, 'Dark routes' is at 55% white, and the disabled 'Dark archive' is at 25% white. The navbar text is at 55% white and its link is white and underlined. The release gives no expand class, so every width shows the collapsed, opened layout the release paints. dark-1280 matches in all respects except the 'Dark routes' finding.

Navbar inverted class (`navbar-dark` inside a light-attribute nav under a dark card), light-1280, light-390, and dark-390: the colors match the white literals in the release's `.navbar-dark` rule. The toggler icon is white through the release's `[data-bs-theme="dark"] .navbar-toggler-icon` rule. The card border, radius, and collapsed layout match. dark-1280 matches in all respects except the 'Dark class routes' finding.

NOT-EVIDENCED: exact pixel values for the stacked link pitch and the overall bar height. The portfolio holds no Bootstrap 5.3.8 reference capture of the same markup to measure against, so this lens rules only on relative placement, color, border, and radius.
